# How Much Does a Commercial Cost to Make? (2026)
URL: https://www.madwackd.ai/producers-corner/how-much-does-a-commercial-cost/
By Zach Wennstedt. Updated 2026-11-06.

Short answer: making a 30-second TV commercial usually costs a few thousand dollars for a simple local spot and $50,000 or more for a national one, before you buy any airtime. One TV ad seller's 2026 guide puts local production at $3,000 to $15,000 and national at $50,000 to $500,000. Airtime is a separate bill.

Every top result for this question is written by someone selling production, and each one quotes its own range. We sell video too, so here's what we did differently: we put the numbers side by side, named where each one comes from, and dated them. Prices change, so check the sources before you sign anything.

## How much does it cost to make a 30-second commercial?

Here's how Simulmedia, a company that sells TV advertising, breaks down production costs in its guide (updated February 2026):

Production cost of a 30-second TV commercial, by type. Source: Simulmedia (a TV ad seller), 2026.
Type of commercial | Typical production cost | 

Local | $3,000 to $15,000 | 

Regional | $15,000 to $50,000 | 

National (standard) | $50,000 to $500,000 | 

Celebrity or premium | $500,000 to $1 million+ | 

Source: Simulmedia, "TV ad production costs" (https://www.simulmedia.com/blog/tv-ad-production-costs) (published May 2025, updated Feb 9, 2026). The guide doesn't say how the ranges were measured, so read them as one seller's estimate, not a survey.

The other production-company guides ranking for this question on November 6, 2026 landed in the same neighborhood: simple local spots in the low-to-mid thousands, polished national spots in the tens of thousands and up. Nobody in the business publishes a neutral, survey-based average, so be wary of anyone who sounds too precise.

## What makes a commercial cost more?

Commercials get expensive for the same reasons movies do: people and days. The big levers:

- Shoot days. Every day on set pays a crew, gear, insurance and food. One day versus three can be the whole difference between a local and a regional budget.

- Talent. Union actors, voice actors and anyone famous cost more, and some contracts pay again each time the ad runs.

- Locations and sets. Your shop is cheap. A closed street, a permit or a built set isn't.

- Music. Licensing a known song can cost more than the shoot. Original or library music is far cheaper.

- Revisions. Each round of changes after the shoot means more editing hours, and reshoots are the most expensive revision there is.

- Versions. A 30-second TV cut, a 15-second cut, and vertical cuts for TikTok and Reels are each extra work.

## How much does it cost to make a 1-minute commercial?

More than double a 30, usually, but not because of the minutes. A longer spot needs more scenes, more setups and more editing, so shoot days and post-production grow. If you only need the length for the web, ask for a 30-second version with a longer online cut made from the same shoot. That's often the cheapest way to get both.

## How much does it cost to air a commercial?

Airtime is billed on top of production, and it swings wildly by market and time of day. Simulmedia's same guide gives these local ranges for a 30-second spot:

Local TV airtime for one 30-second spot. Source: Simulmedia, 2026.
Market size (by DMA rank) | Cost per spot | 

Small markets (151 to 210) | $200 to $1,500 | 

Mid markets (51 to 150) | $500 to $3,000 | 

Large markets (1 to 50) | $2,000 to $10,000 | 

Top 10 markets | $5,000 to $50,000+ | 

At the very top end, CNBC reported that advertisers paid as much as $10 million for 30 seconds during Super Bowl LX in February 2026 (CNBC, Feb 10, 2026 (https://www.cnbc.com/amp/2026/02/10/nearly-125-million-watch-seahawks-crush-patriots-in-super-bowl-lx.html)).

Most small businesses don't start on TV at all. They run the same video as a social ad, where you set the daily budget yourself and can stop anytime.

## Is video worth it for a small business?

The best yearly numbers come from Wyzowl, a video company that has surveyed marketers and consumers for 12 years. Its 2026 report (266 respondents, surveyed late 2025) found:

- 91% of businesses use video as a marketing tool.

- 82% of video marketers say video gives them a good return on investment, down from 93% in 2025.

- 85% of people say a video has convinced them to buy something.

Source: Wyzowl, Video Marketing Statistics 2026 (https://wyzowl.com/video-marketing-statistics/). Wyzowl sells video production, so treat it as an industry survey, not independent research.

## What does an AI-made commercial cost?

AI changes the cost of the camera, not the cost of good ideas. Here's how pricing works at Madwackd Studio, with no crew day involved:

Option | Price | Best for | 

Make it yourself in the studio | Plans from $29/month (see pricing (https://www.madwackd.ai/pricing/)) | Short social ads and clips you direct yourself, with a price shown before every render | 

Done-for-you ad spot | From $2,500 | A finished spot planned, made and revised by a producer | 

Custom music video | From $5,000 | Artists and brands who want a full story, like the two in our Video Vault (https://www.madwackd.ai/vault/) | 

High-end commercial | Quoted, often $20,000 to $30,000+ | Multi-scene campaigns with many versions | 

An honest comparison: an AI clip is not the same thing as a crew-shot national spot with real actors on a real set. What it can do is let a small business test an idea for the price of lunch, then put real money behind the version that works. If you'd rather hand the whole thing off, our human producers (https://www.madwackd.ai/producers/) plan it with you.

## How to keep your commercial budget under control

- Write one sentence first: who it's for, the one thing you want them to do, and why now.

- Decide where it runs before you decide how it looks. A vertical social ad and a TV spot need different shoots.

- Get every price in writing up front, including revisions, music and extra cuts.

- Test small, then scale. Run two or three short versions on social and put the budget behind the winner.

- Plan where the clicks go. An ad that sends people to a slow or confusing page wastes the spend. Search Converts (https://searchconverts.com/?utm_source=madwackd&utm_medium=xpromo&utm_campaign=corner-commercial-cost), part of the Madwackd family, builds landing pages made to turn ad clicks into leads.

Not sure which option fits? Ask Madi, our AI producer (the chat button on every page). Tell her what you sell and your budget, and it will walk you through the options and prices. It's an AI, and it will tell you so.

# How to Make an AI Music Video: How We Made Ours
URL: https://www.madwackd.ai/producers-corner/how-we-made-two-ai-music-videos/
By Zach Wennstedt. Updated 2026-11-06.

Short answer: you can make a music video with AI, but a good one isn't one prompt. Our two music videos, Tell Me Why (4:19) and What Love Really Is (5:01), each took an original song, a locked character design, dozens of AI shots, a frame-by-frame review, retakes, and many rounds of edits by a human producer.

Most guides for "how to make an AI music video for my song" say the same thing: upload your song, pick a style, press go. That gets you a video. It doesn't get you one people watch to the end. Here's what it actually took to make the two music videos in our Video Vault (https://www.madwackd.ai/vault/), written and produced by Zach Wennstedt, the founder of Madwackd Studio. We'll share the process and the lessons. The exact tools and prompts stay in the studio.

Tell Me Why, country music video, 4:19. Written and produced by Zach Wennstedt. A Madwackd Studio production.

## Step 1: Start with the song, then map every line

Both songs were written by Zach. Before making a single picture, we timed every sung line to a fraction of a second with speech-to-text. That timing sheet becomes the edit plan: which shot plays under which words, where the chorus lands, where a cut can hide.

## Step 2: Lock the look before you make shots

The number one problem with AI video is drift: the same character looks like a different person in the next shot. So we make a reference first and hold every shot to it.

- For Tell Me Why, the cowboy is Zach himself, made from his own photos with his consent. (We never make a real person's likeness without their OK. See our trust and safety (https://www.madwackd.ai/trust/) rules.)

- For What Love Really Is, we made a character sheet first: a blue neon crescent moon with a quiff and high-tops, and a pink neon star with a ponytail and boots. Every one of the 25 shots used that sheet as its guide.

## Step 3: Stills first, then motion

Every shot starts as a still picture we approve, then becomes an 8-second moving clip. Stills are cheap and fast to fix. Clips cost more, so you only animate a frame you already like. Tell Me Why used 34 approved stills and 36 clips, cut together in 43 edits.

## Step 4: Check every frame, and retake what's wrong

We sampled frames from every clip and wrote down what broke. Real examples from these two videos:

- A neon star kept turning into a human girl. The cause was one word in the shot description. Removing it fixed the shots.

- Characters doubled, merged into the signs behind them, or picked up readable text that wasn't supposed to be there.

- In the human version of What Love Really Is, the face slowly drifted younger and narrower as he walked toward the camera.

For the neon video, 10 of 25 shots were retaken. Five still glitched after two tries, so instead of forcing them we used their approved still pictures with a slow camera push-in. Viewers can't tell, and the video stays clean.

## Step 5: Know when to drop a feature

We tried AI lip-sync twice on Tell Me Why. It never looked right, so we cut every singing shot. The final video tells the story with looks, hands and horses instead. Sometimes the best fix is removing the thing that doesn't work.

What Love Really Is, neon cartoon music video, 5:01. Written and produced by Zach Wennstedt. A Madwackd Studio production.

## Step 6: Edit like a producer, not a generator

The edit is where these videos came alive, and it's all human judgment:

- Tiny timing fixes. One line in Tell Me Why came in about 3 seconds after the previous one and felt late. We made four test cuts (the original, and 0.5, 1 and 1.5 seconds sooner). Zach picked 0.5 seconds.

- Repeating the best part. The walking chorus was the strongest moment of What Love Really Is, so we brought it back near the end. Making those repeats sound natural took four rounds: we measured where the song's energy and rhythm matched, cut only on the beat, and moved the whispered line onto the first melody.

- Fixing what the viewer notices. A blemish on a close-up, two riders who touch hands for one second and let go (they now hold hands through every horse shot), a hand bent the wrong way. Small things, but they're what makes a video feel finished.

- A whole new look when the first one isn't right. What Love Really Is started as a live-action-style video. Zach wanted something more original, so it was rebuilt as a neon cartoon, and that's the version on our site.

## Step 7: Finish and credit it honestly

Both videos end with a title card: the song name, "Written and produced by Zach Wennstedt," and "A Madwackd Studio production." We don't say "made with one click," because they weren't.

## What this means if you want a music video

If you want… | Do this | 

A few short visual clips for your song's social posts | Make them yourself in the studio (https://www.madwackd.ai/studio/). You see the price before every render. | 

A full music video with characters that stay consistent, a story and a real edit | Hire a Madwackd producer (https://www.madwackd.ai/producers/). Custom music videos start at $5,000. | 

## Common questions

### Can I make an AI music video for my song for free?

You can make short clips with free tools, and many apps offer a free try. A full-length video with consistent characters takes many clips plus retakes, so expect to pay for generation time or for someone's hours. Watch for watermarks and check whether the free plan allows commercial use.

### How do I make an AI video of myself singing?

You need clear, well-lit photos of yourself and a tool that supports likeness with consent. Be ready for lip-sync to be the hardest part: it's where AI music videos most often look wrong. We dropped it entirely on Tell Me Why and told the story without singing shots.

### How long does an AI music video take?

The renders are quick. The review and editing aren't. A one-prompt video can take minutes; a video you're proud of takes many rounds of checking, retakes and edits, often over days.

### Do I have to say it was made with AI?

Platforms like TikTok and YouTube ask about AI-generated content when you upload. Answer honestly. Our AI disclosure (https://www.madwackd.ai/ai-disclosure/) page explains how we label videos.

Got a song? Tell Madi, our AI producer, about it (the chat button on every page). She'll ask a few questions and help you pick between making clips yourself and a full custom video.

# Video Ads for Small Business: A 7-Step Guide
URL: https://www.madwackd.ai/producers-corner/video-ads-for-small-business/
By Zach Wennstedt. Updated 2026-11-06.

Short answer: a small-business video ad works best when it's short, hooks people in the first three seconds, makes one offer, and tells viewers exactly what to do next. TikTok's own guide recommends 21 to 34 seconds for most ads. You can make one with AI for far less than a film crew, then test a few versions before spending real money.

Most "video ads for small business" guides are template galleries. Templates are fine, but they skip the part that decides whether the ad pays off: what you say, in what order, and where the click goes. This guide is the producer's version, built on what the ad platforms themselves publish.

## Why video, and why now?

Video is now the default, not the extra. Wyzowl's 2026 survey found 91% of businesses use video in their marketing, and 41% of marketers paid for video ads this year, up from 36%. 63% of video marketers say they've used AI to make video, up from 51% a year earlier. (Wyzowl, 2026 (https://wyzowl.com/video-marketing-statistics/); Wyzowl is a video company, 266 respondents.)

Small businesses are adopting AI fast too, though the numbers depend on who's asking and how. The U.S. Census Bureau found 19.8% of U.S. businesses used AI in some business function as of May 3, 2026 (Census Bureau, May 2026 (https://census.gov/library/stories/2026/05/ai-use-businesses.html)). The U.S. Chamber of Commerce's 2026 small-business report says two-thirds of small businesses now use AI (U.S. Chamber, Oct 2026 (https://www.uschamber.com/technology/2026-empowering-small-business-report)). Different surveys, different definitions, same direction.

## How long should a small-business video ad be?

For TikTok, the platform says it "recommends 21-34 seconds for most ads" (TikTok for Business video advertising guide (https://ads.tiktok.com/business/en/guides/video-advertising-guide)). Marketers in Wyzowl's survey lean the same way: 71% say videos between 30 seconds and 2 minutes work best. Our advice: make a 20 to 30 second main cut, plus a 6 to 10 second version of just the hook and offer for retargeting.

## How to make a video ad for your small business, step by step

### 1. Pick one customer and one action

"Everyone" isn't a target. Write one sentence: "Homeowners in our area who need X should call us this week because Y." That sentence is your ad.

### 2. Hook them in the first three seconds

TikTok's guide puts it plainly: "Hook viewers in the first three seconds," and skip long intros and logo animations. Open on the problem, the result, or something surprising, not your logo.

### 3. Show, then say

Show the product, the before-and-after, or the moment of relief. Put captions on the screen, because plenty of people scroll with the sound off.

### 4. Make one offer and one call to action

"Book this week, get X" beats a list of everything you do. End with the exact action: call, book, or visit, and show it on screen.

### 5. Make three versions, not one

Change only the hook between versions. Run them side by side with a small daily budget, and move the money to the one that brings in leads, not just views.

### 6. Label AI content honestly

Ad platforms ask you to disclose realistic AI-generated content. On TikTok that's a setting in Ads Manager. Turn it on when it applies. Honest labels don't hurt a good ad, and hiding them can get one pulled.

### 7. Send the click somewhere that converts

A great ad that lands on a slow, confusing page wastes the budget. Make sure the page matches the ad's offer and loads fast on a phone. If you don't have a site that does that yet, Eye To Ad (https://eyetoad.com/?utm_source=madwackd&utm_medium=xpromo&utm_campaign=corner-small-business-ads), part of the Madwackd family, builds websites made to get local businesses found.

## A simple 25-second ad script you can copy

Time | What's on screen | What it says | 

0 to 3 s | The problem, up close | The question your customer is already asking themselves | 

3 to 12 s | You solving it | What you do, in one sentence | 

12 to 20 s | The result or proof | The real outcome (no made-up reviews or numbers) | 

20 to 25 s | Offer + how to act | "Book this week at…" with the phone number or web address on screen | 

## What does it cost to make a video ad with AI?

With Madwackd Studio you can make short ad clips yourself, on plans from $29 a month, and you see the price before anything renders, so there are no surprise bills. If you'd rather not do it yourself, a done-for-you spot starts at $2,500, planned and revised by a producer. Compare that with traditional production in our guide to how much a commercial costs (https://www.madwackd.ai/producers-corner/how-much-does-a-commercial-cost/). Full details are on the pricing page (https://www.madwackd.ai/pricing/).

## Common mistakes to avoid

- Logo first. Nobody stays for a logo animation. Put it at the end.

- Too many messages. One offer per ad. Make another ad for the next offer.

- Fake proof. Invented reviews and testimonials can break FTC rules. Use real customers, with their permission, or skip it.

- Judging too early. Give each version enough spend and days to collect real results before picking a winner.

- Counting views instead of customers. Track calls, bookings and form fills.

Want a script for your business? Ask Madi, our AI producer (the chat button on every page). Tell her what you sell and who you sell to, and it will help you plan your first ad. It's an AI, and it says so.

# Founder's vision: data centers that heat homes and feed people
URL: https://www.madwackd.ai/vision/

The vision, in one line: data centers that heat homes, grow food on their roofs to feed people, and get built with an Earth-first mindset that puts life and the environment before profits. That's our goal. It's not built yet. Here's why I think it can be, and what we're doing right now.

By Zach Wennstedt, founder of Madwackd Productions

## Why I care

I grew up in Boulder, Colorado, hugging trees and getting outside every chance I had. I still do. I have kids, and I think about the world they're going to live in every day.

I also build with AI. Madwackd Studio runs on it. So I can't pretend the computers behind it are free. They use real electricity and they make real heat. The International Energy Agency estimates data centers used about 415 terawatt-hours of electricity in 2024, around 1.5% of the world's total, and expects that to more than double to about 945 TWh by 2030 (IEA, Energy and AI, 2025 (https://www.iea.org/reports/energy-and-ai/executive-summary)).

Almost all of that electricity ends up as heat. Most of it gets blown into the sky. That's the part that drives me nuts, because people need heat. And that's where the idea starts.

## The vision

### 1. Data centers that heat homes

Picture a data center as the furnace for a neighborhood. The servers run, the heat goes into hot-water pipes, and the pipes warm homes, schools and pools. Families pay less to stay warm, and a city burns less coal and gas.

### 2. Gardens on the roof that feed people

Data centers have huge, flat, sunny roofs and a steady supply of warmth. That's a greenhouse waiting to happen. Grow vegetables up there year-round, even in a Colorado winter, and give them to the neighbors, food banks and schools nearby.

### 3. Earth-first from the first drawing

Build it so life and the environment come before profits. Pick the site so the heat has somewhere to go. Use clean power. Save water. Treat the neighborhood like a partner, not a parking lot.

## This is already starting (real examples)

I'm not making this up out of thin air. Parts of it are already working:

Where | What the data-center heat does | Source | 

Odense, Denmark | Heat recovered from Meta's data center goes into the city's district heating, for more than 12,000 homes (2023), running since late 2019. | Ramboll project page (https://www.ramboll.com/projects/energy/meta-surplus-heat-to-district-heating) | 

Tallaght, Dublin, Ireland | A council-owned heat network uses waste heat from a nearby Amazon data center. Operating since 2023, it heats public buildings and 133 apartments, saving an estimated 1,500 tonnes of CO2 a year. | FEDARENE case study (https://fedarene.org/best-practice/turning-data-centre-waste-heat-into-a-public-energy-asset-the-tallaght-district-heating-scheme/) | 

Paris, France | Equinix said in 2024 it would send heat from its PA10 data center to a new neighborhood and the Olympic Aquatic Centre. | Equinix newsroom (https://newsroom.equinix.com/2024-06-05-Help-Us-Heat-Our-Neighbors-Equinix-Makes-Data-Center-Heat-Available-to-Warm-Nearby-Buildings-and-Swimming-Pools) | 

Espoo, Finland (planned) | The city says waste heat from a planned Microsoft data center region will cover about 40% of Espoo's district heating needs in the future. | City of Espoo (https://www.espoo.fi/en/articles/using-waste-heat-new-data-center-cover-40-espoos-district-heating-needs) | 

Governments are pushing too. The EU's Energy Efficiency Directive says data centers over 1 megawatt must use their waste heat unless it isn't technically or economically feasible (Directive (EU) 2023/1791, Art. 26 (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32023L1791)). Germany's Energy Efficiency Act requires new data centers starting from July 1, 2026 to reuse at least 10% of their energy as heat, rising to 20% from July 2028 (EnEfG, German federal law (https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/enefg/__11.html)).

What I haven't found yet is one place that does all three: heats homes, grows food on the roof, and was designed Earth-first from day one. That's the gap. That's the dream.

## What we're doing now (the honest part)

Madwackd is a small studio. We don't own a data center, and I won't pretend we do. Here's what's true today:

- Part of every purchase goes to carbon removal. We contribute 1.5% of our revenue to help advance permanent carbon removal, through Stripe Climate. More on our mission page (https://www.madwackd.ai/our-mission/).

- No wasted renders. Every render is priced before it starts and runs on prepaid credits, so nobody burns compute on surprise or abandoned jobs. That's good for your wallet and for the planet.

- Caps on runaway spending. Budget caps and daily limits stop generation from running away on its own.

## Where we're going

These are goals, not claims. As Madwackd grows, I want to:

- Choose computing partners that reuse their heat and run on clean power, wherever we have a real choice.

- Publish how much we've sent to carbon removal, in plain numbers.

- Make video for environmental and community groups so their stories get seen.

- Someday help build the real thing: a data center that keeps a neighborhood warm and feeds it from the roof.

Life and the environment before profits. That's our goal, and that's my vision. If you're working on any piece of this, a city, a builder, a grower, an engineer, I want to hear from you. Call us at 1-800-481-8638 (https://www.madwackd.aitel:+18004818638).

Zach WennstedtFounder, Madwackd Productions

A personalized creator dashboard and AI production team built around one creator's channel, with every Madwackd studio tool inside and a human producer pass. ## What is the Founding Creator offer?
$99 a month for the first 12 months, then the regular price (today $299 a month). Billed monthly, renews until cancelled, cancel anytime in one click, 14-day money-back on the first payment. Includes every studio tool, the personalized dashboard and production team, a human producer pass, 120 Fast render credits a month (about five 8-second clips; credit packs from $14), 3 Talking Z minutes, one published press release and a Creator Spotlight on madwackd.ai. It is a beta price: the full studio with a smaller render allowance and a direct line to a human producer. Founding rate for the first 100 founding creators or through November 22, 2026, whichever comes first.

## What is a credit, and what is a clip?
Credits pay for render time. A clip is one 8-second AI video shot. Every render shows its exact credit price before you confirm; technical failures are refunded automatically.

## Does it post to my socials for me?
Not yet. Today you cut, caption and export for TikTok, Reels, Shorts, YouTube, Instagram, X, LinkedIn and allofus.one from one panel and share with one tap. Direct posting rolls out platform by platform as each approves the Madwackd app.

## What does the human producer do?
A real producer reviews the dashboard within one business day: brand kit, tone, links and the plan, then approves or fixes it, and drafts the press release for the creator's approval.

## Who owns the work? Are AI clips labeled?
The creator owns their projects; every project comes with a rights pack. AI-generated clips carry an AI label.

## Other tiers
Free Creator Studio tools ($0); Starter $29 and Pro $89 plans; Custom Creator Studio (Studio tier, $299 regular); Genie Production Team $499 (4,800 credits, 3 brand kits, same-day producer pass plus a monthly 30-minute call); done-for-you production from $2,500.

# ElevenLabs vs Madwackd Studio (2026): Voice Platform or Video Studio?
URL: https://www.madwackd.ai/compare/elevenlabs/
Updated: 2026-11-08

Short answer: ElevenLabs is a voice platform. You get audio: text to speech, cloned voices, dubbing, music, sound effects and voice agents, and an image and video product that runs on other companies' video models. Madwackd Studio is a video studio with the voiceover built in: you get a finished clip, you see the credit price before every render, and a human producer is one phone call away. If you need audio files, pick ElevenLabs. If you need a finished video with a voice and a price you can see first, that is what Madwackd Studio is for.

This page is written by the founder of Madwackd Studio, so read it knowing that. Every ElevenLabs fact below comes from elevenlabs.io as it read on November 8, 2026, with no claims beyond what their own pages say. ElevenLabs is a trademark of its owner; we use the name only to identify their product. Prices change; check both pricing pages before you buy.

## What each one actually is

ElevenLabs describes itself around voice: text to speech with 17,500+ voices in 90+ languages (their numbers), voice cloning and voice design, dubbing, speech to text, music, sound effects, a voice-agent platform and an API. Its home page also lists an "Image & Video" product that uses third-party video models. Plans are sold as monthly credits that roughly equal minutes of audio.

Madwackd Studio is an AI video studio from a Denver production company. You describe a shot, the studio shows the credit estimate (seconds x model x takes) before anything renders, you approve it, and the clip comes back with sound. Voiceovers come from a curated set of stock voice styles inside the same project. Real producers run whole projects for people who would rather not do it themselves, and nine free Creator Studio tools run in your browser with no account.

## Side by side

What you care about | ElevenLabs (elevenlabs.io, Nov 8, 2026) | Madwackd Studio | 

What comes out | Audio files; images and video through its Image & Video product | Finished video clips with voice, exported for social and web | 

Price before the job | Monthly credits per plan; no per-job quote described | Credit estimate shown before every render; a budget cap on every project | 

Cheapest way to try | Free plan, 10,000 credits a month (about 10 minutes of audio) | Free Creator Studio tools, no card; $5 Test Drive, 50 credits, one per account | 

Commercial use | Commercial license listed from the Starter plan ($6/mo) up | See the terms of service and acceptable use | 

Voice choice | 17,500+ voices, 90+ languages (their claim) | A curated set of styles: narrator, trailer, upbeat promo, friendly neighbor, documentary | 

Your own voice | Voice cloning and voice design, live | Not offered today; stock styles only. Any custom voice would need a consent check first | 

Consent and rights paper trail | Cloning policies on their site | Consent step before any custom voice; wording, time and a fingerprint of the sample go into the project's rights pack | 

A human you can call | Contact Sales for Enterprise | Producers at 1-800-481-8638; done-for-you spots from $2,500 | 

If the render fails | Not stated on the pricing page | Technical failures with no video refund credits automatically | 

Content labels | See their site | Every clip carries an invisible provenance mark | 

## Where ElevenLabs is bigger

If your job is audio, ElevenLabs has more of everything: more voices, more languages, voice cloning you can use today, dubbing, a developer API and a voice-agent product. Podcasters, app builders, audiobook narrators and anyone building a phone agent should start there. Madwackd Studio does not try to be a general text-to-speech service, and we are still in early access.

# How to Add an AI Voiceover to a Video (2026): A Producer's Guide
URL: https://www.madwackd.ai/producers-corner/ai-voiceover-for-video/
Updated: 2026-11-08

Short answer: write the script for the ear, pick a voice style that matches the job, lock the picture before you generate the final voice, fix pronunciation in the script, place the voice under the video and duck the music, check the license and the AI label, then export per platform. You can do it with a separate text-to-speech tool and an editor, or in one studio that puts the voice on the video and shows you the price before it renders.

Most "add an AI voiceover" guides are three clicks inside one app. Those clicks are the easy part. What decides whether the voiceover sounds like a person or a GPS is the script, the timing and the mix, and those are the same whatever tool you use. This is how our producers do it, in the order we do it.

## Three ways to add an AI voiceover

Way | How it works | Good for | Watch out for | 

Text-to-speech tool + your editor | Generate an audio file, import it, line it up on the timeline | Long narration, podcasts, when you already edit | Timing drift when the picture changes; license terms on free tiers | 

All-in-one video editor | Type the script inside the editor, it drops the voice on the track | Quick social clips from your own footage | Voice quality varies; exports may carry watermarks on free plans | 

Video studio with voice built in | Describe the shot, add the voiceover in the same project, see the credit price, render | Ads, trailers and music videos made from scratch | You pay for render time, so plan the script first | 

Madwackd Studio is the third kind. The steps below work for all three.

## How to add an AI voiceover to a video, step by step

### 1. Write for the ear, not the page

Short sentences. One idea each. Contractions. Read it out loud with a timer: a normal narration pace is roughly 150 words a minute, so a 25-second ad holds about 60 words and an 8-second shot about 20. If you run out of breath, the voice will sound rushed too. The free script fitter in our Creator Studio splits your script into 8-second shots and shows the credit estimate before you spend anything.

### 2. Pick the voice style for the job

Match the voice to the promise. A documentary read sells trust; a trailer read sells scale; a friendly-neighbor read sells a local service; an upbeat promo read sells a deal. Madwackd's stock styles are exactly those five: narrator, trailer, upbeat promo, friendly neighbor and documentary. Generate a test line in two styles and play them to someone who did not write the script.

### 3. Lock the picture first

Change a shot after the voice is done and every line lands late. Finish the cut, or in a studio workflow finish the shot list, then generate the final voice. Rough voice for timing is fine; final voice comes last.

### 4. Generate, listen, fix the script

Most "robotic" problems live in the script, not the voice. Spell numbers the way you say them ("twenty twenty-six"), break acronyms with spaces or periods, and respell brand names phonetically if the voice stumbles. Add a comma where you want a breath. Regenerate only the line you changed.

### 5. Place it and mix it

Voice on its own track, music underneath and ducked so the words stay clear, sound effects where the picture needs them. Most people scroll with the sound off, so add captions as well; the caption maker exports SRT and VTT for free.

### 6. Check the license and the label

Free tiers of voice tools often exclude commercial use, which includes ads and monetized channels. Read the plan before you publish. Ad platforms also ask you to label realistic AI-generated content; some have a setting for it. Madwackd puts an invisible provenance mark on every clip, and any custom voice goes through a consent check first.

### 7. Export for each place it will play

9:16 for Reels, Shorts and TikTok, 16:9 for YouTube and your site. Keep faces and text out of the areas the apps cover; the free safe-zone checker shows where those are.

## Text to speech for YouTube videos: what's different

Longer scripts, so pace matters more. Break a 10-minute script into sections and generate each one, so a late change does not mean regenerating everything. Use one voice for the whole channel so returning viewers recognize it. Faceless channels live or die on the script; a good voice cannot save a flat one. YouTube allows synthetic narration, and its policies on repetitive content still apply, so check the current rules before you build a channel on it.

## What does an AI voiceover for a video cost?

With a standalone voice tool, you pay for audio minutes on a monthly plan and then still need something to make the video. With Madwackd Studio the voice is part of the clip: a Fast 720p shot with sound is about 24 credits, and credits cost $0.10 to $0.14 each depending on plan or pack, so one 8-second shot with voice runs roughly $2.40 to $3.40. The exact quote shows before you confirm, every time. A $5 Test Drive gets you about two shots; plans start at $29 a month. If you would rather hand it off, a producer-made spot starts at $2,500. Full details on the pricing page; results vary by project.

## Mistakes we see most

- Generating the final voice before the cut is locked. Every change after that costs a regeneration.

- One long paragraph. Voices breathe at punctuation. Give them some.

- Using a free voice in a paid ad. Check the license.

- Music louder than the words. Duck it.

- No captions. Most feeds start muted.

## Questions people ask

### Can ChatGPT do voiceovers?

Chat assistants can talk to you, but a video voiceover needs an audio file you can place on a timeline, or a studio that puts the voice on the video for you. Use a text-to-speech tool that exports audio, or a video studio with voice built in. Check the tool's license before using the result in anything you sell or advertise.

### How do I add a voiceover onto a video?

Write the script for the ear, lock your picture edit, generate the voice, listen and fix pronunciation, then place the audio under the video and duck the music beneath it. In Madwackd Studio the voice is added inside the same project as the shot, and the credit price shows before anything renders.

### How can I add an AI voiceover to a video for free?

Several tools have free tiers, and most of them do not include a commercial license, so a free voice is fine for a personal clip and not for an ad. Madwackd's free Creator Studio tools help you write hooks, fit your script to 8-second shots and make captions with no account; the render itself needs credits, from a $5 Test Drive.

### How long should a voiceover script be?

Plan on roughly 150 spoken words a minute at a normal narration pace, so a 25-second ad holds about 60 words and an 8-second shot holds about 20. Read it out loud with a timer; a script that reads well on paper is often too long when spoken.

### Do I have to say a video uses an AI voice?

Ad platforms ask you to label realistic AI-generated content, and some have a setting for it in their ads tools. Madwackd Studio puts an invisible provenance mark on every clip. Check the current rules of the platform you publish on.

# AI Voiceover for Video Ads: Cost, Rights and the AI Label (2026)
URL: https://www.madwackd.ai/producers-corner/ai-voiceover-for-ads/
Updated: 2026-11-08

Short answer: an AI voiceover works in a video ad when the voice style matches the offer, the script is written to be spoken, the plan you generate it on includes commercial use, and you switch on the platform's AI label where the rules ask for it. The voice is the cheap part. A finished 25-second ad with voice costs about $10 to $14 in render credits in Madwackd Studio, quoted before anything renders, or from $2,500 made for you by a producer.

Most pages about "AI voiceover for ads" are written by voice platforms, so they end where the audio file ends. An ad is not an audio file. This guide covers the whole job: picking the voice, writing the read, the rights, the labels each platform requires, and the price of the finished ad. Platform rules below were checked on their own help pages on November 8, 2026 and do change.

## Which voice style for which ad?

Ad | Voice style | Why | 

Local service (plumber, dentist, painter) | Friendly neighbor | You are asking someone to let you into their house. Warm beats slick. | 

Sale, launch, event | Upbeat promo | Energy carries a short offer with a deadline. | 

Product explainer, B2B | Narrator | Clear and even; lets the picture do the selling. | 

Brand film, nonprofit, testimonial-style | Documentary | Slower, lower, trusted. | 

Trailer, game, drop | Trailer | Scale and tension in six seconds. | 

Those five are the stock styles in Madwackd Studio. Whatever tool you use, generate the first line in two styles and play both to someone who did not write the script. They will tell you in one second.

## A 25-second ad script with voice direction

Voice direction is the part most AI-voice guides skip. The same words read three ways are three different ads.

Time | Line (about 60 words total) | Direction | 

0 to 3 s | The question your customer is already asking | Conversational, slightly up at the end. No announcer voice yet. | 

3 to 12 s | What you do, in one sentence | Steady, confident, a touch slower. One breath after the sentence. | 

12 to 20 s | The real result or proof (no invented reviews) | Warm. If it is a number, say it the way people say it out loud. | 

20 to 25 s | The offer and the exact next step | Clear and a little brighter. Phone number or web address also on screen. | 

A normal read runs about 150 words a minute, so 60 words fits 25 seconds with room to breathe. Paste yours into the free script fitter to see how it splits into 8-second shots and what the render would cost.

## Commercial rights, in plain words

A voice you are allowed to use in a personal clip is not always a voice you are allowed to use in an ad. Free tiers on voice platforms commonly exclude commercial use. As one example, ElevenLabs lists a commercial license from its $6-a-month Starter plan up, not on its Free plan, as of November 8, 2026. Read the plan page of whatever you use before the ad goes live, and keep a copy of the license terms with the ad. Madwackd's terms are on the terms of service and acceptable use pages, and every project keeps a rights pack with prompts, versions, consents and receipts.

## The AI label: what each platform requires

### TikTok

Ads Manager has a toggle, "This ad contains AI-generated content". TikTok's help page says it applies when all three conditions are met: it is a TikTok ad, it is not a Spark Ad, and the content "includes image, video, or audio that is either completely AI-generated or significantly modified by AI" (TikTok Ads help). An AI voiceover is audio, so turn it on. Spark Ads follow the organic Community Guidelines label instead. Once submitted, the toggle cannot be removed unless the creative changes.

### Meta (Facebook and Instagram)

For ads about social issues, elections or politics, Meta requires advertisers to disclose photorealistic video or realistic-sounding audio created or edited with generative AI in defined cases, such as depicting a real person saying something they did not say (Meta ad standards). For organic posts, Meta's misinformation policy requires people to disclose realistic-sounding audio that was digitally created or altered. For ads generally, Meta announced that from June 1, 2026 it runs automated detection on ad media and applies an "AI info" label in the About this ad menu with no advertiser action required (Meta newsroom). A plain product ad with an AI narrator is not banned; a realistic fake person or event is where the rules bite.

### YouTube

YouTube requires creators to disclose, through the AI use setting at upload, realistic content generated or meaningfully altered with AI. Its help page lists "cloning one's own voice to create voice overs or dubs" among minor uses that do not need disclosure, and says disclosing "won't limit a video's audience or impact its eligibility to earn money" (YouTube Help). When in doubt, disclose; the label costs nothing and a missed one can.

Madwackd Studio puts an invisible provenance mark on every clip it renders, which supports these labels but does not replace the platform's own toggle. Switch the toggle on yourself.

## What does the finished ad cost?

With a voice-only tool, the voice is a monthly audio plan and the video is a separate bill. In Madwackd Studio the voice is part of the shot. A Fast 720p shot with sound is about 24 credits; a 25-second ad is about four shots, so roughly 96 credits, or $9.60 to $13.44 at $0.10 to $0.14 a credit, before retakes. The exact quote shows before you confirm, every time, and each project has a budget cap. A $5 Test Drive buys about two shots. Plans start at $29 a month. If you would rather hand it off, a producer-made spot starts at $2,500 with script, shots, stock voiceover, 9:16 and 16:9 exports and a revision round. Details on the pricing page; results vary by project.

## Mistakes that get AI-voiced ads ignored or pulled

- Announcer voice on a neighborly offer. Match the style to the promise.

- A free-tier voice in a paid ad. Check the commercial license first.

- Skipping the AI toggle on TikTok. It is a condition of the ad, not a suggestion.

- A fake customer voice. Invented testimonials can break FTC rules, and a cloned real person without consent can break state voice laws. Use real customers with permission, or none.

- Numbers written for the page. "$1,299" reads badly; "twelve ninety-nine" reads like a person.

## Questions people ask

### Can I use an AI voiceover in a TikTok ad?

Yes. TikTok Ads Manager has a toggle, "This ad contains AI-generated content", for ads whose image, video or audio is completely AI-generated or significantly modified by AI. Spark Ads are excluded from the toggle and follow the organic AI-content rules instead. Once submitted, the toggle cannot be unselected unless the creative changes. Checked on TikTok's help page on November 8, 2026.

### Do I have to disclose an AI voiceover in a Facebook or Instagram ad?

For ads about social issues, elections or politics, Meta requires advertisers to disclose photorealistic video or realistic-sounding audio that was created or edited with generative AI in certain cases. For other ads, Meta said that from June 1, 2026 it runs automated detection on ad media and adds an "AI info" label in the About this ad menu, with no advertiser action required. Rules change, so check Meta's current ad standards.

### Does YouTube require a label for an AI voiceover?

YouTube requires disclosure, through the AI use setting at upload, for realistic content that was generated or meaningfully altered with AI. Its help page lists cloning your own voice for voiceovers as a minor use that does not need disclosure, and says disclosing alone does not affect a video's eligibility to earn money. Check the current policy; this reflects November 8, 2026.

### How much does an AI voiceover for an ad cost?

On a voice-only platform you pay for audio minutes on a monthly plan, from free tiers that usually exclude commercial use up to creator plans around $22 a month, then you still need to make the video. In Madwackd Studio the voice is part of the clip: a 25-second ad is about four 8-second Fast 720p shots at about 24 credits each, roughly $9.60 to $13.44 before retakes at $0.10 to $0.14 a credit, and the exact quote shows before you confirm. A producer-made spot starts at $2,500.

### Can I use a celebrity or a famous voice in my ad?

No. Several US states now treat a person's voice as protected, including Tennessee, Illinois and California, and the FTC has proposed extending its impersonation rule to individuals. Madwackd Studio never makes voices of celebrities or public figures, and any custom voice needs the speaker's written consent.

# How Much Does an AI Voiceover Cost? AI vs Voice Actor (2026)
URL: https://www.madwackd.ai/producers-corner/ai-voiceover-cost/
Updated: 2026-11-08

Short answer: an AI voiceover on a voice platform costs from $0 (free tiers, usually without commercial rights) to about $22 a month for creator plans with over 100 minutes of audio, prices checked November 8, 2026. A human voice actor runs about $100 to $500 for a 15 to 60 second commercial on a 2026 marketplace guide, and union TV work starts at a session fee of about $502 plus usage. In Madwackd Studio the voice is part of the video: an 8-second shot with voice is about 24 credits, $2.40 to $3.40, and the exact quote shows before you render.

"How much does an AI voiceover cost" has three honest answers, because there are three different things you can buy: minutes of audio from a voice platform, a human performance priced by usage, or a finished video with the voice already in it. This guide prices all three with sources and dates, then shows when the human is worth the money.

## What you are actually paying for

Option | You pay for | You still need | Typical price | 

Voice platform | Minutes or characters of audio per month | A video, an editor, a commercial-use plan | $0 to $22/mo for creator tiers; $99 and up for pro tiers | 

Human voice actor | A performance, priced by length and where it airs | Casting, direction, a studio or home-studio file, the video | $100 to $500 per short commercial (marketplace); union session about $502 + usage | 

Video studio with voice built in | Render time for the finished shot, voice included | A script and a few retakes | About 24 credits ($2.40 to $3.40) per 8-second Fast 720p shot, quoted first |

Platforms sell audio in credits that roughly equal minutes. ## Human voice actor rates

Human rates are set by usage, not by the minute: the same 30-second read costs more on national TV than on your own website. Numbers you can check:

- A marketplace pricing guide dated March 31, 2026 lists commercials (15 to 60 seconds) at $100 to $500 per project, explainer and corporate narration at $150 to $800, e-learning at $0.10 to $0.50 a word or $20 to $100 per finished minute, and union talent at $2,000 and up per project (Twine, 2026; a freelance marketplace, unattributed ranges).

- The non-union reference most actors quote is the GVAA Rate Guide, which is behind a sign-up and not reproduced here. Expect usage tiers: web-only, local, regional, national.

Budget realistically: a good non-union read for a web ad is a few hundred dollars; a national TV campaign with a known voice is thousands plus residuals. Traditional production costs around the voice are in our guide to how much a commercial costs.

## When a human voice is worth it

- The voice is the brand. A recurring spokesperson, a sound people recognize.

- You need someone to direct. A good actor fixes a weak script in the booth.

For most short social ads, explainers and tests, an AI voice in the right style does the job, and the money is better spent on more versions and more testing.

# Voice Cloning Consent: What You Need Before You Clone a Voice (2026)
URL: https://www.madwackd.ai/producers-corner/voice-cloning-consent/
Updated: 2026-11-08

Short answer: before you clone anyone's voice, get written permission from that person that names the exact uses, the time period and whether they can take it back. Your own voice needs only your own record. Several US states now protect a person's voice by law, including Tennessee, Illinois and California, and the FTC has proposed extending its impersonation rule to individuals. Never clone a celebrity, a public figure or a dead person's voice without the rights holder's consent. This is general information from a video studio, not legal advice.

We wrote this because consent is a hard rule in Madwackd Studio: no custom voice is made until the speaker's permission is confirmed, and that confirmation lives in the project's rights pack. Here is what that permission should look like, what the law says as of November 8, 2026, and a checklist you can copy.

## What counts as consent?

A verbal "sure" is not consent you can rely on. Consent you can show someone later has five parts:

- Who. The speaker's name and signature, and a statement that the voice is theirs.

- What for. The specific uses: which videos, which channels, whether ads are included, whether the clone can say new words or only re-record a script.

- How long. A time period, and what happens to the voice model and the sample when it ends.

- Take-backs. Whether the speaker can revoke it, and how.

- Money. Any payment, or a clear statement that there is none.

California's AB 2602 sets a useful bar even outside California: a contract provision for a digital replica of a performer's voice or likeness is enforceable only if it describes the intended uses with reasonable specificity, or the performer was represented by counsel or a union (Covington, Sept 2024). "Any use, forever" is exactly the clause the law was written against.

## The laws that now protect a voice

This is not a complete list, and the details are for a lawyer. These are the ones a creator or a small business should know exist.

Law | What it does | Source | 

Tennessee, ELVIS Act (HB 2091), enacted March 2024 | Adds voice to the state's right of publicity; prohibits knowingly distributing an unauthorized digital replica, and reaches tools whose primary purpose is making them | Covington | 

Illinois, HB 4875, signed August 2024 | Amends the Right of Publicity Act: no knowingly distributing a sound recording or audiovisual work that contains an unauthorized digital replica of a person's voice, image or likeness | IPWatchdog | 

California, AB 2602 and AB 1836, signed September 17, 2024 | AB 2602: digital replica contract terms must specify uses and the performer must be represented. AB 1836: no commercial digital replicas of deceased performers without the estate's consent | Governor of California | 

Federal, FTC impersonation rule, February 2024 | Final rule on impersonating government and businesses; a supplemental proposal would extend it to impersonating individuals, citing AI voice cloning | FTC | 

Federal, NO FAKES Act (proposed) | Would create a federal right over your own digital replica; introduced in the Senate July 31, 2024 and not law as of this writing | Covington | 

Other states have passed or are moving on similar bills. If your business or your speaker is in a state not listed, assume a similar rule exists and get consent anyway. It costs a page of paper.

## Who you can never clone

- Celebrities and public figures, including politicians, with or without a disclaimer.

- Deceased people, without the estate's written consent (California's AB 1836 is explicit).

- Anyone, to make them say something they did not say in a realistic way. Platforms treat that as manipulated media and the laws above treat it as an unauthorized replica.

- A customer or employee from a recording you happen to have. Having the audio is not having the permission.

## What the platforms ask for

Separate from the law, the places you publish have rules. YouTube requires disclosure of realistic AI-generated or altered content through its AI use setting, lists cloning your own voice for voiceovers as a minor use that needs no disclosure, and may penalize creators who consistently fail to disclose (YouTube Help). TikTok's Ads Manager requires its AI-generated content toggle on ads whose audio is completely AI-generated or significantly modified by AI (TikTok Ads help). Meta requires disclosure of realistic-sounding altered audio in organic posts and in social-issue, election and political ads (Meta policy). The label rules for ads are in our AI voiceover for ads guide.

## How Madwackd Studio handles it

Today the studio's voiceovers come from stock voice styles, so no one's real voice is cloned. Any custom voice, when it is offered, goes through the consent step first: you confirm it is your own voice or that you hold written permission from the speaker, and you name them. The wording, the time and a fingerprint of the sample go into the project's rights pack, which you can download as CSV or PDF alongside prompts, versions, model IDs and receipts. We never make voices of celebrities or public figures. Details on the Voice and Trust and safety pages.

## Consent checklist you can copy

- Speaker's full name and signature, with the date.

- "This is my voice" statement, or the speaker's authority to grant rights to it.

- Exact uses: project names, channels, ads yes or no, new words yes or no.

- Territory, if it matters to you.

- Time period and what happens to the model and sample afterwards.

- Revocation: whether, how, and how fast you will stop.

- Payment, or none.

- A copy of the sample recording, with its date.

- Who holds the file and where (your rights pack, your contracts folder).

- A line that the speaker is over 18, or a parent or guardian's signature.

## Questions people ask

### Is it legal to clone my own voice?

Cloning your own voice for your own videos is the clear case: you are the speaker and you consent. YouTube even lists cloning your own voice for voiceovers as a minor use that needs no disclosure. Keep a record that it is your voice, and read the platform's terms on what it may do with your sample. This is general information, not legal advice.

### Can I clone a celebrity voice for a parody or a joke?

Do not. Tennessee's ELVIS Act, Illinois' HB 4875 and California's digital replica laws now treat a person's voice as protected, and parody is not a safe harbor you should bet an ad on. Madwackd Studio never makes voices of celebrities or public figures.

### Do I need consent to clone an employee's or a client's voice?

Yes, in writing, naming the uses, the time period and whether it can be revoked. California's AB 2602 requires that contracts for digital replicas describe the intended uses with reasonable specificity. Treat that as the standard everywhere.

### What should a voice consent form include?

The speaker's name and signature, a statement that it is their voice, the exact uses (which videos, which channels, ads or not), the time period, whether it can be revoked and how, any payment, and a copy of the sample. Madwackd Studio stores the consent wording, time and a fingerprint of the sample in the project's rights pack.

### What can I do if someone clones my voice without permission?

Document it, report it to the platform where it appears (YouTube, TikTok and Meta all take reports on synthetic media), and talk to a lawyer about your state's right-of-publicity or digital replica law. The FTC's impersonation rule covers businesses and government today and the agency has proposed extending it to individuals.

Want a voice without the paperwork? The stock styles need no consent form, and the price shows before every render. Start for $5, or call 1-800-481-8638.
